title: Postcomposition comparison for raw coherent realization
statement:
Use quasicategories, weak homotopy equivalences and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the canonical mapping-space composition and homotopy category $hS$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and coherent realization and locally Kan replacement of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $S$ be a small quasicategory, put $D=\mathfrak C[S]$, and write $r:D\to RD$ for an object-preserving locally Kan replacement. Let $W=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RD)$ and $a:S\to W$ be adjoint to $r$. Then $a$ is a categorical equivalence, and for every pair of vertices its map $\operatorname{Map}_S(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_W(ax,ay)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. For every edge $h:y\to z$ and every vertex $w$, the composite of this map with the inverse of the locally Kan comparison $RD(w,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_W(aw,ay)$, interpreted in the homotopy category of spaces, carries postcomposition by $h$ to enriched postcomposition by the vertex $r([h])$. Here $[h]$ denotes the vertex of $D(y,z)$ induced by that edge.

Consequently, whenever $h\circ-:\operatorname{Map}_S(w,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_S(w,z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, the actual simplicial composition map $[h]\circ-:D(w,y)\to D(w,z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Moreover the assignment sending an edge $h$ to the component of $[h]$ induces an isomorphism $hS\cong\pi_0D$, fixing objects and respecting composition. In particular every isomorphism in $\pi_0D$ is represented by an equivalence edge of $S$. No local Kan hypothesis on $D$ is imposed.

source.place: HTT Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 2.2.4.1; replacement and composition comparison used in Proposition 3.2.2.10. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result; HTT is requested in report.md.

proof.text: Write $M_T(x,y)=\operatorname{Map}_T(x,y)$. The replacement theorem gives $r:D\to RD$ inducing weak homotopy equivalences $r_{xy}$ on mapping sets. The map from the empty simplicial set to $S$ is a monomorphism, so $S$ is Joyal-cofibrant. The locally Kan category $RD$ is Bergner-fibrant: its map to the terminal category is locally a Kan fibration and the identity lifts the only target isomorphism. Apply the defining criterion of the cited Quillen equivalence to the adjoint pair of maps $r:\mathfrak C[S]\to RD$ and $a:S\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}RD$. Since $r$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence (including on components, with objects fixed), $a$ is a categorical equivalence. The coherent-nerve theorem makes $W$ a quasicategory. Equivalence detection then says that $\mathfrak C[a]$ is Dwyer--Kan, so each $\mathfrak C[a]_{xy}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: HTT Theorem 2.2.5.1, Quillen equivalence criterion, and Proposition 2.2.5.8.

proof.text: Apply the pinched-rigidification resolution to both quasicategories $S$ and $W$. For $f=a_*:M_S(x,y)\to M_W(ax,ay)$ its naturality gives the strictly commutative square $\theta_W\,|f|_Q=\mathfrak C[a]_{xy}\,\theta_S$. Both $\theta$ maps are weak homotopy equivalences by that node; the mapping-set map on the right is one by Step 1. Thus $|f|_Q$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The same node supplies natural weak homotopy equivalences $p_K:|K|_Q\to K$, and $p_{M_W}|f|_Q=f p_{M_S}$. Two-out-of-three now gives that the actual map $f=a_*$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. These applications of two-out-of-three are elementary: on components and on each based homotopy group the two displayed equalities are equalities of functions or homomorphisms with the other factors invertible.

source.place: HTT Proposition 2.2.4.1 and the natural maps of Section 2.2.2; explicit two-square argument.

proof.text: Let $h:y\to z$ and fix $w$. Set $k=r([h])$, and denote the coherent-nerve mapping comparison by $b_{wv}:RD(w,v)\simeq M_W(aw,av)$. It sends the vertex $k$ to $a(h)$: on $\Delta^1$ the adjunction evaluates the single generating arrow under $r$. For the Hom bifunctor, the natural transformation induced by $a$ at the edge $(1_w,h)$ gives $a_{wz,*}(h\circ-)=(a(h)\circ-)a_{wy,*}$ in the homotopy category of spaces. The coherent-nerve composition clause gives $(a(h)\circ-)b_{wy}=b_{wz}(k\circ-)$. Hence, writing $t_{wv}=b_{wv}^{-1}a_{wv,*}$, we obtain $t_{wz}(h\circ-)=(k\circ-)t_{wy}$. The inverse exists because $b$ is a weak equivalence, and Step 2 shows each $t$ is an isomorphism. This is precisely the asserted comparison, including its specified vertex and endpoints.

source.place: HTT coherent-nerve comparison; coherent Hom naturality and enriched-composition clauses of the cited nodes.

proof.text:
Suppose $h\circ-$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 3 identifies the map $k\circ-$ between the Kan complexes $RD(w,y)$ and $RD(w,z)$ with conjugation of this equivalence by the isomorphisms $t$. It is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence: the maps on components and all based homotopy groups are conjugate by isomorphisms, with basepoint paths supplied by the comparison homotopies. Since $r$ is a simplicial functor, there is also the strictly commutative square
$$r_{wz}([h]\circ-)=(k\circ-)r_{wy}.$$
Both $r_{wy}$ and $r_{wz}$ are weak homotopy equivalences by the replacement statement. Taking components and based homotopy groups in this equality proves that the actual simplicial map $[h]\circ-:D(w,y)\to D(w,z)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This last argument uses neither Kan-ness of $D(w,y)$ nor Kan-ness of $D(w,z)$.

source.place: Agent deduction from Step 3 and strict functoriality of r; not an application of HTT Proposition 3.2.2.10.

proof.text: On each hom-set define $F:hS\to\pi_0D$ by $[h]\mapsto\pi_0([h])$. To check well-definedness and bijectivity, use the resolution zigzag $M_S(x,y)\leftarrow |M_S(x,y)|_Q\to D(x,y)$. Both arrows induce bijections on components, and its degree-zero clause says both take the vertex indexed by an edge $h$ to that edge or to $[h]$. Thus the resulting bijection is exactly $F$. The mapping-composition and Hom-functoriality statements give a functor $ha:hS\to hW$. The coherent-nerve comparison identifies $\pi_0RD$ with $hW$ respecting composition, while $\pi_0r:\pi_0D\to\pi_0RD$ is an isomorphism fixing objects. On every edge, these two functors composed with $F$ agree with $ha$, by the vertex calculation in Step 3. Injectivity of their hom-set maps therefore forces $F$ to preserve identities and composition. It is an isomorphism since its hom-set maps are bijective and it fixes objects. Every morphism of $hS$ has an edge representative, and the mapping-composition statement says an invertible class is represented by an equivalence edge. Apply this to $F^{-1}$ of an isomorphism in $\pi_0D$. Only $RD$, not the raw realization $D$, was assumed locally Kan.

source.place: Agent deduction using the degree-zero clause of HTT Proposition 2.2.4.1 and composition compatibility.
